title: Scalar compatibility of the diagonal base-change factor
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings, φ:A→B a unital map, and N>0 an integer killing both rings. Let X,Y be Noetherian schemes with N invertible on Y, and f:X→Y a separated quasi-compact compactifiable smooth morphism of pure relative dimension d. Write D_A(f) for finiteSmoothDiagonalFactor A f, the inverse section compositor for Δ followed by Δ* of the canonical dualizing base-change map for the self-product of f [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Write c_f for the unit-normalized exceptional coefficient map [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-tensor-maps], and q_(p1,Δ) for scalar/pullback balancing followed by pullback of c_p1 [def-pur-dnc-coefficient-section-maps]. Then Q_X(D_A(f)) ≫ q_(p1,Δ) = c_f ≫ D_B(f). This compares only the base-change factor; no DNC map, integration or supplied smooth orientation occurs.

proof.text: The source-library boundedConstructibleFiniteTor_dualizingComplex theorem applies to f because the common annihilator N is invertible on Y and therefore on X. It is a consequence of smooth tensor duality: omega_f is a shifted locally constant free rank-one sheaf. Its boundedness supplies the source D+ input. The scalar_extension_plus_of_finiteTor calculation from ExceptionalCoefficientComparison supplies the scalar D+ input, using the finite Tor amplitude of omega_f and the scalar tensor comparison. No flatness of B over A is required.

Work with the flipped self-product Cartesian square, whose upper map is the second projection and whose structural map is the first projection. The existing compact_scalar_exchange_left calculation gives the compact-support scalar square on the two D+ inputs. Invert its isomorphisms and cancel the vertical chosen compact-support scalar comparisons to obtain coefficientPullbackSquare for inverse exchange. The two exceptional maps have the mate counit equations, as do the two coefficient mates. Apply coefficient_exchange_of_counit_at. This proves the exceptional scalar/base-change square for this arbitrary Cartesian presentation, directly rather than via the standard chosen-pullback predicate.

Evaluate the exceptional square at the coefficient unit. Naturality of the exceptional scalar mate moves the pulled-back A-unit comparison through the coefficient mate. etaleScalarPullback_unit identifies scalar extension of that unit comparison followed by the target scalar unit with inverse scalar/pullback balancing followed by pullback of the source scalar unit and the B-pullback unit. Naturality of the B exceptional base-change transformation then identifies the two paths with the specified dualizingScalarMap and dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap composites. This is the private dualizing_scalar_square calculation.

Pull the dualizing square along the diagonal. Naturality of the inverse scalar/pullback comparison moves the A base-change map past balancing. The scalar_section_compositor equation, after cancellation of its section compositor, identifies scalar extension of the inverse A compositor followed by the two balancing maps with the inverse B compositor. Naturality of that inverse B compositor at the dualizing coefficient map completes the equation. The private scalar_section_factor lemma proves this categorical cancellation, and unfolding only finiteSmoothDiagonalFactor and the two names for the unit-normalized coefficient map yields the statement unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSmoothDiagonalScalar
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0) (hB : (N : B) = 0)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [HasCompactification f] [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] :
    (ordinaryScalar φ X).map (finiteSmoothDiagonalFactor A f) ≫
        WeilConjectures.DncCoefficientTransport.sectionMap φ
          (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f) =
      ExceptionalCoefficients.dualizingScalarMap φ f ≫
        finiteSmoothDiagonalFactor B f
